append.text: **Ps 87:9b *óculi mei languérunt præ inópia* → *os meus olhos se enfraqueceram de penúria*** — draft 1 had 43:24's *carência*; **the stylist and the ambiguity reader both heard it as emotional lack ('carência afetiva')**, the fault already noted for *carente* at 85:1. *penúria* (the stylist's) taken there and **proposed for the row** (43:24 and 106:41 to follow, if ruled); *carência* option. Passed the v2 Latinist.

**Ps 87:14 *et mane orátio mea prævéniet te* → *e de manhã a minha oração vos precederá*** — the friendly transitive the row named as its next test. Draft 1 had the row's *se adiantará a vós*; the stylist called it unidiomatic (the second stylist to refuse it, after 58:10) and the ambiguity reader heard 'outrun you'. **Proposed: friendly transitive → *preceder*** (58:10 *me precederá* should follow; 20:4 decides); hostile *surpreender* (17:19) and 16:13 *adiantai-vos a ele* untouched. Cost: *præcédere* (96:3) will need another word. The R. of the Sunday Prime preces reads alone. Passed the v2 Latinist.

**Ps 87:5 *Æstimátus sum cum descendéntibus in lacum* → *Fui contado entre os que descem à cova*** — a local departure: 'reckoned among a company', not 'regarded as' (43:22b). The Latinist and the stylist both asked for *contado*; the ambiguity reader did not know *tido*. The row stands where the sense is 'regarded as'. The Latinist's *com* (for *cum*) held twice as an option.

**Ps 87:19 *Elongásti a me amícum et próximum* → *Pusestes longe de mim o amigo e o próximo*, and 87:9 *Longe fecísti notos meos a me* → *Pusestes longe de mim os meus conhecidos*** — one Greek verb (ἐμάκρυνας) in both, one Portuguese phrase (D15; 39:12). No reader asked for *afastar* this time; *Afastastes* (MS1932) is the option.

**Ps 87:18 *circumdedérunt me simul* → *cercaram-me ao mesmo tempo*** — the row's option, the stylist's (draft 1 *cercaram-me juntos* was clipped at the final, and its masculine gave the unnamed subject a gender). The v2 Latinist (minor) found it narrower than 'together' and asked *todos juntos*; held, option.
Ps 87:5 *descendéntibus in lacum* → *os que descem à cova* (the formula); 87:7 *in lacu inferióri* → *na cova mais baixa* (the *inferióra terræ* row's comparative-as-superlative).
Ps 87:12 *Numquid narrábit áliquis in sepúlcro* → *Acaso alguém narrará no sepulcro*; the stylist asked *contará* (the r-a run, 'literary') — refused for the row, option.
Ps 87:9, 87:19 *notos meos* → *os meus conhecidos* — applied; no reader remarked.

**Ps 87:15 *Ut quid, Dómine, repéllis oratiónem meam* → *Por que, Senhor, repelis a minha oração*** and 87:6 *de manu tua repúlsi sunt* → *foram repelidos da vossa mão* (the same Greek, ἀπωθέω; *de manu*, not *a me*, so the row's verb). No reader remarked on either.

**Ps 87:4 *et vita mea inférno appropinquávit* → *e a minha vida se aproximou do inferno*** — kept; the ambiguity reader heard the hell of the damned first, as foreseen (the realm of the dead is meant, as 29:4).
**Ps 87:8 *Super me confirmátus est furor tuus* → *Sobre mim se firmou o vosso furor*** (ἐπεστηρίχθη = 70:6); MS1932 and DM1962 *pesou* (the Hebrew) refused. No reader remarked.
Ps 87:11, 12, 13 → *Acaso* three times (the Latin has three, not five); no reader remarked.

terms: | languére | enfraquecer-se (*os meus olhos se enfraqueceram*) | open | Ps 87:9b, the only *languére* in the psalms (Psalmorum grep). The Greek is ἠσθένησαν, infirmári's verb (9:4, 30:11b, 108:24 → *enfraquecer*), so D15 merges them. The stylist asked *definharam*; option. |

| prex | prece (*inclinai o vosso ouvido à minha prece*) | working | Ps 87:3 (δέησις), 39:2 *preces meas* → *as minhas preces*. Shares *prece* with deprecátio (D35); the two do not meet in either verse. *súplica* option. |

| tenebrósa (neuter plural as noun) | lugares tenebrosos (*nos lugares tenebrosos, e na sombra da morte*) | open | Ps 87:7 (σκοτεινοῖς; DRB 'dark places', MS1932). A noun supplied; *nas trevas* refused (ténebræ follows in 87:13). The ambiguity reader did not know *tenebrosos*. |

| perdítio (a place) | perdição (*e a vossa verdade na perdição*) | open | Ps 87:12 (ἀπώλεια, parallel to *sepulcro*). The ambiguity reader heard damnation first; *destruição* is intéritus's. *no lugar da perdição* (DM1962) option. |

| médici (87:11) | os médicos (*ou os médicos os ressuscitarão*) | open | Ps 87:11 (ἰατροί; the Hebrew has 'shades') — the Latin kept (rule 1, DRB, MS1932); the object pronoun supplied because intransitive *ressuscitar* would make the physicians rise. The ambiguity reader heard doctors and found it strange — the Latin's own strangeness. |

| liber (*inter mórtuos liber*) | livre (*livre entre os mortos*) | open | Ps 87:5 (ἐλεύθερος; the Fathers' reading of Christ). MS1932 *abandonado* (the Hebrew's sense) refused; the ambiguity reader found it puzzling, perhaps positive — the Latin's crux, kept. |
formulas: | *Intret orátio mea (*) in conspéctu tuo(, Dómine): inclína aurem tuam ad precem meam* (87:3; Saturday minor-hours antiphon, Psalmi minor; Introit of Quad1-6, with 87:2 *Dómine, Deus salútis meæ: in die clamávi, et nocte coram te*, also its Offertory) · *V. Et ego ad te, Dómine, clamávi. R. Et mane orátio mea prævéniet te* (87:14; Sunday Prime preces, Preces.txt) | *Que entre na vossa presença a minha oração: * inclinai o vosso ouvido à minha prece* · *Senhor, Deus da minha salvação: * de dia clamei, e de noite diante de vós* · *V. E eu clamei a vós, Senhor. R. E de manhã a minha oração vos precederá* | open — Ps 87; each colon reads alone. 87:3 took *Que* before *entre* (bare *Entre* was heard as 'between' by two readers); 118:170 *Entre … na vossa presença* stands mid-psalm |
